'''Petr Beckmann''' (November 13, 1924 – August 3, 1993) was a professor of [[electrical engineering]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Frazier |first=Mark |date=1977-04-01 |title=Spotlight: Petr Beckmann |url=https://reason.com/1977/04/01/spotlight-petr-beckmann/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=Reason.com |language=en-US}}</ref> and advocate of [[libertarianism]]<ref name=":0" /> and [[nuclear power]]<ref name=":0" /> who  disputed [[Albert Einstein]]'s [[theory of relativity]] and other accepted theories in [[modern physics]].

==Biography==
In 1939, when Beckmann was 14, his family fled their home in [[Prague|Prague, Czechoslovakia]] to escape the [[Nazism|Nazis]]. From 1942 to 1945, he served in a [[Czechs|Czech]] squadron of the [[Royal Air Force]]. He worked as a radar mechanic on the newly invented radar systems that helped Britain win the Battle of the Atlantic.<ref>Access to Energy, Vol. 20, no. 2; October 1992</ref>   He received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] in 1949, a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1955, and a [[Doctor of Science|D.Sc.]] in 1962, all from [[Prague]]'s [[Czech Academy of Sciences]] in [[electrical engineering]].  He [[Defection|defected]] to the [[United States]] in 1963 and became a professor (later, [[emeritus]]) of [[electrical engineering]] at the [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado]]. In the United States, he became acquainted with novelist [[Ayn Rand]], a contributing editor to a publication devoted to her ideas, ''[[Objectivist periodicals#The Intellectual Activist|The Intellectual Activist]]'', and a speaker at The Thomas Jefferson School, an intellectual conference of similar purpose.

Beckmann was a prolific author; he wrote several electrical engineering textbooks and non-technical works.  By 1968, he had founded Golem Press, which published most of his books. The Golem Press books included ''The Health Hazards of Not Going Nuclear'' (1976), which argued in favor of [[nuclear power]] during the height of the [[anti-nuclear movement]] by making "apples-to-apples" comparisons of the risks of nuclear power with the risks in the same terms (e.g., deaths per terawatt hour) of the alternative power sources.  Beckmann also wrote ''[[A History of Pi|A History of {{math|π}}]]'', documenting the history of the calculation of {{math|[[pi|π]]}}. The book also expresses opposition to the Roman culture, [[Catholic Church|Catholicism]] (and other [[religion]]s), [[Nazism]], and [[Communism]]. He published his own monthly newsletter, ''Access to Energy'', which since September 1993 has been written by biochemist [[Art Robinson|Arthur B. Robinson]].

In 1981, he took early retirement with emeritus status, in order to devote himself fully to what he saw as the defense of science, technology and [[Free market|free enterprise]], through his newsletter, ''Access to Energy''. He founded the Golem Press in 1967, publishing more than nine books. These included ''The History of {{math|π}}'', ''Einstein Plus Two'', and ''The Health Hazards of Not Going Nuclear'' (with an Introduction by [[Edward Teller]]). He wrote some 60 scientific papers and eight technical books. Beckmann spoke at the 1990 San Francisco Conference of [[Liberty International (organization)|International Society for Individual Liberty]] (ISIL), where he received a standing ovation for his speech in which he attacked "sham environmentalists".<ref>Freedom Network News, [http://www.rkba.org/libertarian/isil/fnn/fnn04.txt Obituaries – Dr. Petr Beckmann, 1924–1993] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304031805/http://www.rkba.org/libertarian/isil/fnn/fnn04.txt |date=2016-03-04 }} (Fall 1993).</ref>

Beckmann was also a frequent participant in [[Usenet]] debates. In them, he claimed to have debunked [[Albert Einstein]]'s theory of [[special relativity]] in his book ''Einstein Plus Two'', as well as in the journal ''Galilean Electrodynamics'', which he also founded.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farrell |first=John |date=2000-07-06 |title=Did Einstein cheat? |url=https://www.salon.com/2000/07/06/einstein/ |access-date=2022-03-25 |website=Salon |language=en |archive-date=2022-03-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325193729/https://www.salon.com/2000/07/06/einstein/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
